items.summary: Traditional unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) methods are designed to flag or localise deviations from a normative distribution, ignoring the underlying generative mechanisms of the anomalies. Yet the nature of an anomaly is often as important as its presence. We reformulate UAD as a Bayesian inverse problem, in which the objective is to infer the most probable corruption responsible for each observation. Our framework yields a probabilistic anomaly score as the energy of the inferred corruption parameters, and serves as a principled recipe for developing new UAD algorithms. We derive several existing methods as instances of the general framework, each corresponding to the same energy score under different modelling choices. Experimentally, we study the framework's components in a controlled setting, and improve object-class AUROC on the MVTec AD dataset by 2.3% by adapting the underlying corruption model. Finally, we validate the framework on a brain MRI benchmark, achieving strong detection performance while producing estimates of pathology intensity, bias, and geometry. Code is available at https://github.com/jgmyles/inverse-uad.
items.title: A Principled Approach to Unsupervised Anomaly Detection

items.summary: Memory segmentation is thought to arise from rapid decorrelation in neural activity, often quantified by Euclidean distance or cosine angle. Although these metrics detect a transition, they do not reveal how the new state relates to the repertoire represented by the neural manifold. This matters because neuromodulators that drive state transitions also alter excitability, and learning may repurpose existing representations or create new ones. Here, I introduce a geometric decomposition that separates changes attributable to gain modulation of a nearby manifold state from movement within the manifold and genuine off-manifold displacement. The approach uses the radial axis of neural population activity to partition the normal space of a local manifold region. A central challenge is identifiability: given only a static reference manifold and a single test state, neither the state from which a perturbation began nor its gain magnitude and mechanistic decomposition can generally be recovered uniquely. I therefore formulate identifiability as a cascade of geometric gates specifying when each component can be interpreted. The gates distinguish structural failures, including the absence of a local chart or incorrect intrinsic dimensionality, from estimation error and systematic bias caused by reference sampling, tangent-frame error, gain-axis misalignment, anchor displacement, and poor ratio conditioning. Simulations show that neighborhood size, curvature, sampling density, ambient dimension, and noise act through a small set of geometric quantities. The framework specifies when assignments to gain or novelty are identifiable, how they become biased, and which diagnostics reveal the relevant failure regime. By quantifying the nature rather than only the magnitude of neural state change, it provides a clear, readily interpretable framework for evaluating mechanisms of neural state transitions.
items.title: Identifying Neural State Changes due to Gain versus Off-Manifold Displacement

items.summary: Discovering the structure and kinetics of chemical reaction networks (CRNs) from time-series concentration data is a fundamental challenge in chemical kinetics, with existing approaches relying on prior mechanistic assumptions or suffering from high computational cost and noise sensitivity. In this work, we present integral chemical reaction neural networks (iCRNNs), a framework that combines the interpretable, physics-constrained, architecture of chemical reaction neural networks (CRNNs) with an integral collocation formulation of the governing dynamics. Rather than solving ODEs forward in time at each training step, we approximate the integral of the learned rate functions directly using numerical quadrature. This yields an entirely algebraic forward pass consisting only of matrix operations, eliminating the repeated adaptive ODE solves of standard CRNN and producing smoother, more predictable training. We provide a recovery error analysis characterising the structural sources of ill-conditioning (conservation laws, reaction reversibility, and shared reactant sets) that limit network identifiability. On two benchmark CRNs, iCRNN trains in roughly half the wall-clock time of the baseline CRNN method on a four-species mechanism and between three and four times faster on a five-species mechanism, while completing every training run reliably and attaining comparable or lower loss.
items.title: Integral chemical reaction neural networks

items.summary: Activation steering has become a widely used approach for controlling language models during explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, motivating its extension to latent CoT. However, we find that steering continuous thoughts produces substantially weaker effects on subsequent language generation than steering explicit CoT, even when the hidden representations are moved by comparable amounts. We first show that task information remains identifiable in continuous thoughts. Hence, we hypothesize a \textbf{latent-to-language transition gap}, in which an intervention effect in latent space fails to transfer to language generation. Two further results support this hypothesis: the output distribution changes abruptly at the transition boundary, and task-related directions exert much weaker bidirectional control in latent CoT than in explicit CoT. These findings identify the transition interface as a central target for evaluating and designing future latent-steering methods.
items.title: When Steering Fails in Latent Reasoning: A Latent-to-Language Transition Gap

items.summary: Generative world models offer controllable and repeatable closed-loop simulation for end-to-end and vision-language-action driving policies, but production deployment exposes three unresolved requirements: faithfully reproducing a mixed fisheye-pinhole rig at native resolutions; reconciling causal, per-timestep interaction with long-horizon stability and low latency; and preserving scene identity when a location is revisited. We present ZYT-World, a single architecture that natively generates four fisheye views with field of view > 180° and three pinhole views. Projection-specific Plucker adapters encode camera geometry, ego-motion adaptive layer normalization provides global motion control, and a lightweight pixel-aligned layout conditions traffic participants and signals through instance-level boxes, headings and colors. Heterogeneous training combines full-rig geometric coverage with high-resolution detail. Teacher forcing, causal consistency distillation, self-rollout distribution matching distillation, and RigCritic transform a 40-step bidirectional teacher into a one-step, per-latent streaming generator, with RigCritic evaluating the seven-view rig jointly. A 19M-parameter variational autoencoder decoder (TinyVAE), W8A8 quantization, and our inference engine reduce decoding, backbone, and incremental-execution costs, respectively. Finally, cross-trajectory pairs derived from real captures train a plug-in implicit-memory module that preserves place-specific evidence. On the internal multi-view test set, the one-step model retains more than 90% of the teacher's PSNR and SSIM, while FID, FVD, and LPIPS stay within 11% of the teacher. Under the generator-only timing in Figure 2, it is 107.7 times faster than the 40-step bidirectional teacher. TinyVAE decodes 59.8 times faster than Wan. 30s rollouts and cross-trajectory revisits show the intended long-horizon and memory behavior.
items.title: ZYT-World: A Real-Time Controllable World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous-Driving Simulation

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) provide limited support for sign language interaction. Unifying sign language translation (SLT) and generation (SLG) to enable sign language as both input and output can reduce switching between separate models during sign-text interaction. We present SignGPT, a unified, pose-based framework for gloss-free SLT and SLG. SignGPT integrates part-aware hierarchical representations of body, hand, and facial motion into a shared language model and employs asymmetric multi-token prediction and progressive training for bidirectional modeling. We evaluate SignGPT on How2Sign (ASL) and Phoenix-2014T (DGS) through benchmark comparisons, qualitative analyses, and component ablations. An exploratory study with 12 Deaf ASL signers assesses an LLM-mediated sign-to-sign response pipeline, highlighting the potential of unified modeling to support sign language conversation (SLC).
items.title: SignGPT: Toward LLM-Mediated Sign Language Interaction through Gloss-Free Translation and Generation

items.summary: Reproducibility release 1.1.0 for Ocean Engineering manuscript OE-D-25-10458. This package supports a controlled Rotterdam-Yokohama comparison of the Suez, Cape and Northern Sea Route corridors using three predefined strategic waypoint philosophies per corridor. The archive contains the Python routing and analysis code, all nine waypoint definitions, frozen maritime-network geometries and scenario/leg distances, dual-coastline quality-assurance and local-repair reports, 0.05/0.025-degree convergence outputs, sourced OpenStreetMap Suez Canal geometry and provenance, downstream time/fuel/CO2 analyses, exponent and vessel-reference sensitivities, and the frozen manuscript sources and figures. The routing method uses searoute 1.4.3, WGS84 distance recomputation and no great-circle fallback. The reproduction command stages the archived routes, regenerates downstream tables and copies the included figure assets. A full routing rerun additionally requires the externally distributed Natural Earth 10 m v5.1.1 and GSHHG 2.3.7 full L1 coastline datasets. Tests and release checks are documented in the archive. The comparison is strategic and does not predict realised voyages or commercial viability.
items.title: Effects of Route Representation on Distance and Downstream Voyage Implications in Europe–Asia Trade: A Comparison of the Suez, Cape, and Northern Sea Route Corridors

items.summary: We prove that a finite poset with at most fifteen elements, width at most three, and the following common-incomparability property has at most 48 antichains: for every x < y, the elements incomparable with both x and y form a chain of size at most two. An explicit fifteen-element poset attains the bound. We show that order-six stable-marriage rotation posets satisfy these hypotheses by examining convex rotation blocks and their fixed partner pools. This gives a structural upper bound of 48 stable matchings, matching the lower bound already provided by Benjamin, Converse, and Krieger in 1995. Equality forces fifteen rotations, all of size two, and every one of the 36 man–woman pairs occurs in some stable matching. Provenance note: This preprint is accompanied by reproducible verification artifacts and a partial Lean formalization. The Lean development verifies the finite-poset core and supporting components; it does not formalize the entire stable-marriage theorem f(6) = 48 end to end. The source-code and reproducibility repository is available at https://github.com/insammael/stable-marriage-f6 and is linked as a related resource.
items.title: Small Rotation Blocks and the Order-Six Stable Marriage Problem

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. Keywords distributed version control; Git; agentic software development; evidence engineering; provenance; content addressing; Merkle DAG; software agents; developmental trajectories; negative knowledge; residual primacy; FRF; FRF-Fuzz; reproducibility; software archaeology; semantic lineage; source provenance; event sourcing.
items.title: Gemel: Evidence-Native Version Control for Agentic Software Development - Longitudinal Engineering Memory, Residual-Aware Change Graphs, Git Interchange, and Reproducible Agent Handoffs

items.summary: Documentation/provenance synchronization release for the reproducibility software supporting confidence-aware, risk-calibrated, multiobjective tuning of an edge-executable battery-supported microgrid energy-management system. The scientific evidence chain remains frozen; this patch synchronizes the published Zenodo identifiers, manuscript v10 provenance, and archival metadata without changing experimental results.
items.title: Confidence-Aware Robust Edge EMS: Reproducibility Software for Risk-Calibrated Multiobjective Tuning

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of tasks, motivating two important aspects of deployment: inference efficiency and output provenance, which can be tackled by speculative sampling and watermarking, respectively. However, recent works have shown that combining these two goals is highly nontrivial and can be potentially impossible. In this work, we develop a novel multi-draft speculative sampling algorithm based on Poisson processes that improves the frontier of this fundamental trade-off. The proposed algorithm has strong sampling efficiency on its own and, more interestingly, is naturally watermarkable: we can embed an unbiased watermark without degrading speculative acceptance. Moreover, our algorithm is based on an exact list-coupling-without-communication scheme, which yields a drafter invariance property that benefits both sampling and watermarking. It is the first multi-draft, drafter-invariant speculative sampling scheme that maintains both watermark strength and sampling efficiency, and we experimentally verify its strong performance in both aspects.
items.title: Watermarkable Multi-Draft Speculative Sampling via Poisson Processes

items.summary: Weekly, hashed copy of the verifiable-silence observations Crovia Trust publishes at croviatrust.com/registry/tacet/ : 17 signed hourly epoch sheets (13 anchored in Bitcoin), 1,260 observed AI models, 1,149 negative snapshots and 19 silence proofs in the crovia.seal.v1 receipt format. A silence proof shows, for one model, that in every observed hour no training-data disclosure matching the published predicate appeared on its public surfaces: a sparse-Merkle non-inclusion path per epoch, the drand round that opened the epoch and the OpenTimestamps receipt that closed it. Proofs verify offline with pip install crovia-tacet-operator crovia-seal or in the browser at croviatrust.com/registry/seal/verify/ . Crovia records what was observed and what was not; it does not grade, rank or attribute intent. Durations are bounded by observed hours. Weekly summary: Silence Report 2026-W38 . Definitions: CANON.md . Receipt format: IETF draft-crovia-seal . Licence CC-BY-4.0. Cite the series by the Concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20111130.
items.title: Crovia — Verifiable silence observations of AI training-data disclosure, weekly snapshot 2026-W38

items.summary: Abstract Modern enterprise AI systems increasingly operate across multiple authorized data sources, memories, applications, and tools. This creates a security problem that is not adequately described as conventional data theft. An AI workload may be individually authorized to read support records, engineering information, source-control activity, supplier data, budgets, hiring information, and calendars. No individual source may contain a sensitive strategic conclusion. However, the AI system may combine those independently authorized fragments and reconstruct a new high-value object: an unreleased product direction, likely launch window, supplier dependency, market strategy, organizational weakness, or other forward-looking enterprise knowledge. The security boundary therefore changes. The relevant questions are no longer only: Who may read data A? or: Who may read data B? They also become: Who may establish the relationship A-to-B? Who may retain or disclose the resulting inference? Who may cause an external action because of that reconstructed meaning? This paper describes a threat model in which the AI assistant becomes a computational graph across previously separate enterprise systems. The resulting risk may exist even when each underlying retrieval complies with its ordinary source-level permissions. The sensitive object is not necessarily a stolen database record; it may be a new semantic object created through authorized association. The architecture therefore separates two security transitions: Authorized Data | v Authorized Reconstruction | v Computed Meaning | v Authorized Effectuation | v External Consequence The first transition concerns association authority : permission to read independently authorized fragments does not automatically imply permission to join those fragments into a new semantic relationship. The second concerns execution-time finality : permission to compute, generate, or prepare an output does not automatically imply permission for that output to become externally consequential. The proposed architectural model therefore introduces controls around independently governed relationship mapping, session-bound reconstruction, minimum-necessary temporary views, provenance-aware release, and a mandatory effectuation boundary. Candidate outputs or actions remain non-effective until the consequence-controlling component verifies the applicable authority, provenance, destination, policy state, disclosure conditions, and other protected execution state immediately before release or effectuation. In compact form: Access != Association Association != Authority to Disclose Computation != Authority to Cause Consequence The execution-time consequence boundary may be implemented through existing mechanisms such as policy-enforcement points, reference monitors, authorization servers, secure execution environments, transaction coordinators, capability systems, protected dispatchers, database commit controls, network command gates, or equivalent mechanisms. The important property is functional rather than terminological: A computed result or proposed action remains non-effective until the component with mandatory control over the actual consequence verifies that the exact pending effect is permitted under current protected authority and state. This architecture is intended to complement conventional identity, access control, encryption, zero-trust, data-loss prevention, confidential-computing, logging, and authorization systems rather than replace them. Those mechanisms continue to protect identities, stores, channels, and individual permissions. The additional problem addressed here is governance of the relationship created between authorized fragments and governance of the transition from computed meaning to actual consequence . The paper presents this as a forward-looking threat model rather than an allegation concerning any specific enterprise or AI product. The objective is to identify an architectural risk
items.title: Enterprise AI as a Reconstruction Layer: Governing Derived Knowledge and Execution-Time Consequences

items.summary: Preconditioned Total Field Inversion: a single-step method that inverts the total field directly to susceptibility over the whole field-of-view, jointly performing background-field removal and dipole inversion. Uses a preconditioner (χ = P·y, larger outside the brain) so the large out-of-brain background susceptibility is well-conditioned, with MEDI-style L1 morphology regularization. QSM-CI reconstruction method tfi-qsmrs . Browse and run it at https://qsmxt.github.io/QSM-CI/submission.html?method=tfi-qsmrs .
items.title: QSM-CI method: TFI (QSM.rs) (v4)

items.summary: Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme is a cumulative collection of mathematical papers, complete LaTeX proofs, formalization sources, calculations and literature-based research notes. Its central question is how the zeros of the Riemann zeta function can be studied through explicitly constructed arithmetic cohomology, spectral actions and quantitative metric estimates. The collection also retains the related heat-flow, arithmetic-trace, fluid, complexity and thermal-geometry investigations from which parts of this programme developed. Project and reading guide · Research contents · Machine-readable workbench index . Papers remain separate readable PDFs; the source archives supply the corresponding editable mathematics and supporting materials. What the collection contains Split-Zero coefficients, geometry and cohomology. The construction retains a ring's internal zero and a separate symbol for absence, so a zero element in a specified support fibre is not confused with an absent fibre. The papers construct coefficient maps, quotients, homology, finite spectral jets and their relation to the infinite theta quotient. Deligne's Weil II provides a motivating source for the cohomology–duality–weight-control programme; its finite-field theorem is not asserted to apply automatically to the Riemann zeta function. Read the cohomology and weight-control paper and the foundational objects and maps . Arithmetic theta sources and analytic control. The central analytic complex is [V → B], with theta map Θ and quotient B/ΘV. Scaling acts by D = −x∂x; the Mellin-side arithmetic function is 2ξ(s), where ξ is the completed Riemann zeta function. The papers carry finite zero packets, including multiplicities, through the original source maps and least-norm quotient metrics. They develop source recovery, residue and period maps, tensor and exterior constructions, Mellin and Gamma estimates, orthogonal-polynomial kernels, Hankel–Toda determinant identities, boundary terms, and growing-degree volume and covariance calculations. The cumulative Split-Zero reader , its proof companion , and the separate kernel, conductor and source-transport papers retain the complete arguments. Conductor geometry and spectral observation. Further papers calculate the original relation and conductor maps, kernels, quotient volumes, real-period resonances, inverse spectra and finite observation bounds. The native spectral paper , real-period paper , resonance-direction paper and inverse-power observation paper have distinct, explicit scopes. Geometric examples are not represented as identified arithmetic zeta-zero packets. Formalization and reproducible calculation. The Lean sources and formalization notes cover specified algebraic, quotient and homological interfaces. Source packages retain exact finite checkers, numerical or interval calculations where supplied, figures, manifests and verification records. A Lean check of an interface, a finite algebra test and an analytic proof are documented as different forms of evidence; none silently certifies the others. The wider zeta literature and connected investigations. The separate zeta reader , fluid/Navier–Stokes reader , de Bruijn–Newman heat-flow reader , Connes/arithmetic-trace reader , geometric-complexity reader and vacuum and thermal-geometry reader preserve the earlier research routes and their stated limitations. Related Unified Flow calculations concern specified black-hole, thermal, spectral-zeta and geometric-flow probes. The CUE research map connects existing random-unitary-matrix, Mellin and finite-phase-space work. An analogy or proposed connection is not presented as an established implication between major conjectures. How to read and assess the work This is an ongoing research programme, not a claimed proof or disproof of RH or the other major conjectures discussed in the connected notes. The remaining arithmetic estimates and identifications are stated in the individual paper
items.title: Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme

items.summary: This work presents reusable mathematical bridges extracted from the Chronos formal-verification programme and related Lean developments in constrained dynamics, quantum mechanics, gravity, operator theory, partial differential equations, and Yang–Mills theory.   The purpose of the work is to make formally developed mathematical structures available for reuse beyond the physical problems in which they were originally constructed.   The paper develops four primary reusable connections.   First, it presents an internal-time framework for constrained Hamiltonian systems. When a candidate clock has a nonvanishing rate along a constrained trajectory, the system can be reparameterized with respect to that clock, producing relational evolution. This connects directly with the existing Chronos frozen-to-flow and Wheeler–DeWitt formalization.   Second, it develops a quantum–classical shared-time bridge based on expectation-value evolution. For suitable Hamiltonians, including the constant-force system already treated in the formal programme, quantum expectation values obey exact classical equations of motion.   Third, it extracts a reusable operator-theoretic chain connecting coercive lower bounds to positive spectral bounds, invertibility, and quantitative inverse or resolvent control. Together with cutoff and graph-core machinery developed during the Yang–Mills formalization, this provides reusable infrastructure for unbounded operators in quantum mechanics and partial differential equations.   Fourth, it presents the general inverse-distance field structure underlying the existing Chronos gravity formalization. A radial inverse-distance potential produces an inverse-square gradient, satisfies the three-dimensional vacuum Laplace equation away from the source, and has radius-independent spherical flux. The same mathematical structure can therefore be instantiated in Newtonian gravity, electrostatics, Green-function theory, and other potential problems.   The central goal is compositional reuse. Rather than treating each formal proof as an isolated endpoint, the work identifies intermediate machine-checkable theorem structures that can serve as starting points for additional formal developments.   Immediate applications include relational clock models, Wheeler–DeWitt and constrained systems, Ehrenfest and semiclassical quantum dynamics, electrostatic inverse-square fields, Schrödinger operators, spectral-gap arguments, elliptic PDEs, gauge systems, and other operator-theoretic problems.   This paper accompanies the broader Chronos formal-verification programme and is intended as an openly reusable mathematical and formal-physics resource.
items.title: Reusable Formal Bridges from Chronos Verification: Internal Time, Quantum–Classical Dynamics, Operator Control, and Inverse-Distance Fields

items.summary: We investigate Floquet--spin-orbit compensation in the three-band $α$-$T_3$ system, which interpolates between graphene at $α=0$ and the dice lattice at $α=1$. By tuning the interplay between an off-resonant circularly polarized optical field and intrinsic spin--orbit coupling, we identify three distinct pairwise band-degeneracy conditions in the quasienergy spectrum: (i) valley--spin degeneracy, (ii) spin--band degeneracy, and (iii) flat--dispersive band degeneracy. The flat band is not an artifact of a two-band reduction but rather an exact property of the continuum Hamiltonian at this compensation point, where the complete three-band Hamiltonian supports a momentum-independent dark state. A winding-two low-energy Hamiltonian and a finite-momentum Berry-curvature maximum, whose radius scales as the square root of the detuning, emerge from detuning this contact. We further show that the intrinsic transverse thermoelectric response encodes these spectrum patterns. The flat- and quadratic-band degeneracy can be predicted for $0<α<1/2$ because the two response scales linked to the linear contacts have a monotonic ratio independent of the common spin--orbit energy scale. This allows an inverse determination of $α$ and of the common spectral scale. The analytical results are confirmed by full three-band Kubo calculations, which also define the regime in which this inverse characterization is still observable. These results connect an experimentally accessible, Berry-curvature-sensitive thermoelectric response to tunable Floquet--spin--orbit band geometry.
items.title: Floquet-spin-orbit compensation and flat- and quadratic-band contact in the $α$-$T_3$ lattice

items.summary: Discovering the structure and kinetics of chemical reaction networks (CRNs) from time-series concentration data is a fundamental challenge in chemical kinetics, with existing approaches relying on prior mechanistic assumptions or suffering from high computational cost and noise sensitivity. In this work, we present integral chemical reaction neural networks (iCRNNs), a framework that combines the interpretable, physics-constrained, architecture of chemical reaction neural networks (CRNNs) with an integral collocation formulation of the governing dynamics. Rather than solving ODEs forward in time at each training step, we approximate the integral of the learned rate functions directly using numerical quadrature. This yields an entirely algebraic forward pass consisting only of matrix operations, eliminating the repeated adaptive ODE solves of standard CRNN and producing smoother, more predictable training. We provide a recovery error analysis characterising the structural sources of ill-conditioning (conservation laws, reaction reversibility, and shared reactant sets) that limit network identifiability. On two benchmark CRNs, iCRNN trains in roughly half the wall-clock time of the baseline CRNN method on a four-species mechanism and between three and four times faster on a five-species mechanism, while completing every training run reliably and attaining comparable or lower loss.
items.title: Integral chemical reaction neural networks

items.summary: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) have attracted extensive attention in recent years due to their strong capability for high-quality 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis from multi-view images. Existing methods usually rely on high-quality sharp inputs, while real-world image acquisition is highly susceptible to blur degradation, which severely affects the reconstruction quality of NeRF. In this paper, we propose a novel Mamba-driven world-state-aware adaptive deblurring neural radiance field, termed WS-NeRF, to address image degradation and 3D inconsistency. We formulate the alternating optimization of radiance fields as a dynamic evolution process with temporal memory, and jointly exploit comprehensive multi-dimensional world states and a mixture-of-experts mechanism to dynamically adjust the confidence of deblurring priors. Experimental results show that WS-NeRF significantly improves blurry radiance field reconstruction quality, achieving better performance on PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, while exhibiting more stable iterative recovery behavior.
items.title: WS-NeRF: A Mamba-Driven World-State-Aware Adaptive Deblurring Neural Radiance Field

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. items.summary: Code and frozen experimental data accompanying the accepted JCDL 2026 paper A Provenance-First Discovery Layer for Research Gaps, Limitations, and Future Directions in ETDs . The system proposes research-gap, limitation, and future-direction passages from electronic theses and dissertations, aligns retained passages to source text and physical PDF pages, and keeps proposed type and synopsis separately reviewable. Version 1.0.0 includes the implementation, prompts, schemas, evaluation tools, and 31,486 frozen data files: compiled source text and corpus metadata, study splits, model outputs, reference construction, passage audits, the 600-record human-review ledger, training traces, and expected results. The code archive and checksum-pinned data archive support CPU reproduction of the reported statistics, including the original 20,000-resample whole-ETD bootstrap intervals. Fresh model training, inference, and external audits are separate operations; source PDFs and model weights are not included. The GitHub repository provides installation instructions, result lineage, validation receipts, and documented reproduction limits: provenance-first-etd-discovery . License scope: MIT applies to original project software; CC BY 4.0 applies to original generated data. Third-party ETD text, quotations, metadata, and separately licensed material retain their existing rights. These licenses do not relicense third-party source content; see LICENSING.md.
items.title: A Provenance-First Discovery Layer for Research Gaps, Limitations, and Future Directions in ETDs — Code and Data

items.summary: Reproducibility archive for a fully computational study of a coupled interface-mode multilayer sensing refractive index and temperature over a 100 K range, accompanying the article "Bias-Aware Detection Limits, Calibration Transfer and Matched-Control Robustness Assessment in Dual-Parameter Photonic Refractive-Index and Temperature Sensing: A Coupled Interface-Mode Multilayer Case Study" by Agah Oktay Ertay and Muhammed Mustafa Ertay, accepted by Sensors (MDPI) on 18 September 2026. Version 1.2.1 is the publication release. It carries version 1.2.0, which the Data Availability Statement of the article names, without changing any number, table, input, model, or analysis script (560 of 572 files byte for byte; the 12 replaced root documents are kept under provenance/v1.2.0/). It adds the figure artwork as published: every graphic of the article and of its Supplementary Material as supplied to the journal (figures/published/), the source that draws the 20 graphics redrawn at the proof stage for typographic reasons (true minus signs, notation, legend placement; code/publication_figures/, with a complete diff against the production source), and a launcher mode that re-renders them from the archived tables. It contains the MATLAB production forward model and driver scripts, the frozen material, geometry and acceptance-criterion input files, and the sensitivity matrix, nonlinear calibration, covariance and probability-of-detection routines, the per-realization Monte Carlo yield and matched-control output tables, the design-search evaluation log, the FDFD, CST, MEEP, MPB and FEniCSx verification models with their exported spectra and convergence histories, and the numerical series behind every figure and table in the article and in its Supplementary Material. Version 1.2.0 adds the analyses of the major revision as a separately runnable stage that uses the archived production routines and the frozen tables of version 1.1.0: the sensitivity of the detection limits to instrument noise and drift, reduced per-device calibration protocols, the complete metric set of the nanolaminate-free stack, an oblique-incidence test of the hyperbolicity condition, and the jointly matched trivial control with its paired benchmark. The 483 source, input, result, figure, and solver files of version 1.1.0 are carried byte for byte; only the root metadata files and the launcher were updated, and the v1.1.0 metadata and checksum manifest are kept under provenance/v1.1.0/. A single launcher runs the integrity check, the full reproduction, the revision stage, or both; a SHA-256 manifest covers every other file in the archive. Code is released under the MIT License (LICENSE-CODE); data, result tables, and figures under CC-BY-4.0 (LICENSE-DATA). The three measured ITO n,k tables are third-party public-domain data (CC0 1.0, via refractiveindex.info, originating from Minenkov et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 16, 9517-9531, 2024) and should be cited from that source. The study is numerical. No multilayer was fabricated and no spectrum measured; agreement between independent solvers is not offered as experimental validation.

items.summary: Memory segmentation is thought to arise from rapid decorrelation in neural activity, often quantified by Euclidean distance or cosine angle. Although these metrics detect a transition, they do not reveal how the new state relates to the repertoire represented by the neural manifold. This matters because neuromodulators that drive state transitions also alter excitability, and learning may repurpose existing representations or create new ones. Here, I introduce a geometric decomposition that separates changes attributable to gain modulation of a nearby manifold state from movement within the manifold and genuine off-manifold displacement. The approach uses the radial axis of neural population activity to partition the normal space of a local manifold region. A central challenge is identifiability: given only a static reference manifold and a single test state, neither the state from which a perturbation began nor its gain magnitude and mechanistic decomposition can generally be recovered uniquely. I therefore formulate identifiability as a cascade of geometric gates specifying when each component can be interpreted. The gates distinguish structural failures, including the absence of a local chart or incorrect intrinsic dimensionality, from estimation error and systematic bias caused by reference sampling, tangent-frame error, gain-axis misalignment, anchor displacement, and poor ratio conditioning. Simulations show that neighborhood size, curvature, sampling density, ambient dimension, and noise act through a small set of geometric quantities. The framework specifies when assignments to gain or novelty are identifiable, how they become biased, and which diagnostics reveal the relevant failure regime. By quantifying the nature rather than only the magnitude of neural state change, it provides a clear, readily interpretable framework for evaluating mechanisms of neural state transitions.
items.title: Identifying Neural State Changes due to Gain versus Off-Manifold Displacement

items.summary: This software package contains the code used for the simulation, analysis, and reproducibility of a study on closed-loop digital-twin validation of federated learning updates for methane control in underground mining. The package includes the plant–twin simulator, federated-learning routines, calibration scripts, intervention-budget analyses, attack calibration and backdoor diagnostics, candidate-update generation and scoring, the fresh-seed confirmatory analysis, twin-mismatch sensitivity experiments, exploratory Krum-based comparisons, FLTrust-style diagnostics, serious-harm analyses, and read-only manuscript audits. The evaluation separates the simulated plant used for operational outcome assessment from the imperfect digital twin used for candidate scoring. The repository also documents the distinction between direct plant evaluation and curve-interpolated budget matching used in different experimental stages. Raw methane measurements are not redistributed in this archive. The study uses the public dataset “Methane” by Sikora and Wróbel, available from Mendeley Data, Version 1, DOI: 10.17632/yd7vw4c5mk.1. Instructions for obtaining and preparing the data are provided in DATA.md. The archive includes reproducibility documentation, script-to-manuscript mapping, provenance notes, execution order, software requirements, and SHA-256 checksums. Historical scripts are retained where necessary to document the progression from early exploratory analyses to the final frozen analysis.
items.title: SFDT-DTVRA: Reproducibility Code for Closed-Loop Digital-Twin Validation of Federated

items.summary: Documentation/provenance synchronization release for the reproducibility software supporting confidence-aware, risk-calibrated, multiobjective tuning of an edge-executable battery-supported microgrid energy-management system. The scientific evidence chain remains frozen; this patch synchronizes the published Zenodo identifiers, manuscript v10 provenance, and archival metadata without changing experimental results.
items.title: Confidence-Aware Robust Edge EMS: Reproducibility Software for Risk-Calibrated Multiobjective Tuning

items.summary: Reproducibility release 1.1.0 for Ocean Engineering manuscript OE-D-25-10458. This package supports a controlled Rotterdam-Yokohama comparison of the Suez, Cape and Northern Sea Route corridors using three predefined strategic waypoint philosophies per corridor. The archive contains the Python routing and analysis code, all nine waypoint definitions, frozen maritime-network geometries and scenario/leg distances, dual-coastline quality-assurance and local-repair reports, 0.05/0.025-degree convergence outputs, sourced OpenStreetMap Suez Canal geometry and provenance, downstream time/fuel/CO2 analyses, exponent and vessel-reference sensitivities, and the frozen manuscript sources and figures. The routing method uses searoute 1.4.3, WGS84 distance recomputation and no great-circle fallback. The reproduction command stages the archived routes, regenerates downstream tables and copies the included figure assets. A full routing rerun additionally requires the externally distributed Natural Earth 10 m v5.1.1 and GSHHG 2.3.7 full L1 coastline datasets. Tests and release checks are documented in the archive. The comparison is strategic and does not predict realised voyages or commercial viability.
items.title: Effects of Route Representation on Distance and Downstream Voyage Implications in Europe–Asia Trade: A Comparison of the Suez, Cape, and Northern Sea Route Corridors

items.summary: Reproducibility software for confidence-aware, risk-calibrated, multiobjective tuning of an edge-executable battery-supported microgrid energy-management system under finite simulation budgets and distribution shift. items.title: Confidence-Aware Robust Edge EMS: Reproducibility Software for Risk-Calibrated Multiobjective Tuning

items.summary: We prove that a finite poset with at most fifteen elements, width at most three, and the following common-incomparability property has at most 48 antichains: for every x < y, the elements incomparable with both x and y form a chain of size at most two. An explicit fifteen-element poset attains the bound. We show that order-six stable-marriage rotation posets satisfy these hypotheses by examining convex rotation blocks and their fixed partner pools. This gives a structural upper bound of 48 stable matchings, matching the lower bound already provided by Benjamin, Converse, and Krieger in 1995. Equality forces fifteen rotations, all of size two, and every one of the 36 man–woman pairs occurs in some stable matching. Provenance note: This preprint is accompanied by reproducible verification artifacts and a partial Lean formalization. The Lean development verifies the finite-poset core and supporting components; it does not formalize the entire stable-marriage theorem f(6) = 48 end to end. The source-code and reproducibility repository is available at https://github.com/insammael/stable-marriage-f6 and is linked as a related resource.
items.title: Small Rotation Blocks and the Order-Six Stable Marriage Problem

items.summary: README – Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics (CGMD) Simulations of PIEZO1 and TRPM4 Overview This dataset contains coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 and the non-mechanoprotective ion channel TRPM4 embedded in lipid bilayers. The simulations comprise 500 ns of equilibrium followed by membrane stretching simulations designed to investigate how PIEZO1's distinctive triskelion blade architecture redistributes mechanical stress and preserves membrane integrity. All simulations were performed using GROMACS with the Martini 3 force field. Independent replicate simulations (n = 3) were conducted for each system to ensure statistical robustness and reproducibility. Simulation Details Parameter Description Molecular dynamics engine : GROMACS v2021.2 Force field : Martini 3 Membrane model : Lipid bilayer containing either PIEZO1 or TRPM4 Equilibration : 500 ns Stretching simulations : Three independent replicates (n = 3); 50 ns Simulation temperature, pressure, and all additional parameters are provided in the accompanying simulation input files (.mdp) and described in the associated publication. Biological Significance PIEZO1 is a mechanosensitive ion channel whose unique triskelion blade architecture protects cellular membranes from mechanical failure. Its extended peripheral blades redistribute mechanical stress across the lipid bilayer, reducing localized stress accumulation and delaying membrane rupture during mechanical loading. This dataset enables quantitative investigation of how membrane protein architecture influences membrane mechanics, force redistribution, and mechanoprotection using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. Dataset Structure 1. Equilibrium Simulations These simulations characterize the equilibrated membrane environment surrounding each ion channel before mechanical loading. Simulation length: 500 ns PIEZO1_equilibrium.pdb PIEZO1_equilibrium.xtc TRPM4_equilibrium.pdb TRPM4_equilibrium.xtc 2. Membrane Stretching Simulations Following equilibration, membrane stretch was induced using semi-isotropic pressure coupling, with −5 bar applied in the membrane plane (x–y) while maintaining +1 bar normal to the bilayer (z-axis) using the Parrinello–Rahman barostat. PIEZO1 PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.edr PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.edr PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.edr TRPM4 TRPM4_Stretch_R1.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R1.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R1.edr TRPM4_Stretch_R2.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R2.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R2.edr TRPM4_Stretch_R3.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R3.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R3.edr Data Usage The trajectory (.xtc) and coordinate (.pdb) files can be analysed using standard molecular dynamics software, including GROMACS, VMD, and PyMOL. The (.edr) files are also provided for energy calculations and to be utilized -b 0 -e 50000 (time 0 - 50 ns) These simulations support quantitative analyses described in the associated publication. PIEZO1 safeguards membranes under mechanical stress via permeation-independent structural adaptation and calcium-dependent cytoskeletal reinforcement. Cell Press Blue. (2026). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpblue.2026.100128
items.title: PIEZO1 safeguards membranes under mechanical stress using MD simulation

items.summary: Self-contained synthetic seismic–gravity inversion models, Python operators, seeds, archived and profile-initialized fits, regional controls, posterior samples, figures and validation records for the manuscript by Emilson P. Leite and Maiara M. Gonçalves. Version 0.11 adds a four-start calibration on 96 paired noise comparisons, an audit of unchanged displayed seismic median errors, exact n=32 coverage intervals, and empirical bias–variance accounting of the existing regional controls. The four-start shortcut did not reproduce the profile solutions; the manuscript retains 32 profile-initialized noise pairs for each free-geometry configuration. Fixed-geometry ensembles retain 256 realizations. Wide local intervals under a free trend coexist with systematic target-property errors directed towards the prior. No new posterior chains were generated in this revision. Field observations and third-party BP-model data are not required.
items.title: When gravity adds useful information to interpretation-conditioned post-stack seismic inversion: reproducibility archive

It contains the MATLAB production forward model and driver scripts, the frozen material, geometry and acceptance-criterion input files, and the sensitivity matrix, nonlinear calibration, covariance and probability-of-detection routines, the per-realization Monte Carlo yield and matched-control output tables, the design-search evaluation log, the FDFD, CST, MEEP, MPB and FEniCSx verification models with their exported spectra and convergence histories, and the numerical series behind every figure and table in the article and in its Supplementary Material. Version 1.2.0 adds the analyses of the major revision as a separately runnable stage that uses the archived production routines and the frozen tables of version 1.1.0: the sensitivity of the detection limits to instrument noise and drift, reduced per-device calibration protocols, the complete metric set of the nanolaminate-free stack, an oblique-incidence test of the hyperbolicity condition, and the jointly matched trivial control with its paired benchmark. The 483 source, input, result, figure, and solver files of version 1.1.0 are carried byte for byte; only the root metadata files and the launcher were updated, and the v1.1.0 metadata and checksum manifest are kept under provenance/v1.1.0/. A single launcher runs the integrity check, the full reproduction, the revision stage, or both; a SHA-256 manifest covers every other file in the archive. Code is released under the MIT License (LICENSE-CODE); data, result tables, and figures under CC-BY-4.0 (LICENSE-DATA). The three measured ITO n,k tables are third-party public-domain data (CC0 1.0, via refractiveindex.info, originating from Minenkov et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 16, 9517-9531, 2024) and should be cited from that source. The study is numerical. No multilayer was fabricated and no spectrum measured; agreement between independent solvers is not offered as experimental validation.

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. Keywords distributed version control; Git; agentic software development; evidence engineering; provenance; content addressing; Merkle DAG; software agents; developmental trajectories; negative knowledge; residual primacy; FRF; FRF-Fuzz; reproducibility; software archaeology; semantic lineage; source provenance; event sourcing.
items.title: Gemel: Evidence-Native Version Control for Agentic Software Development - Longitudinal Engineering Memory, Residual-Aware Change Graphs, Git Interchange, and Reproducible Agent Handoffs

items.summary: Discovering the structure and kinetics of chemical reaction networks (CRNs) from time-series concentration data is a fundamental challenge in chemical kinetics, with existing approaches relying on prior mechanistic assumptions or suffering from high computational cost and noise sensitivity. In this work, we present integral chemical reaction neural networks (iCRNNs), a framework that combines the interpretable, physics-constrained, architecture of chemical reaction neural networks (CRNNs) with an integral collocation formulation of the governing dynamics. Rather than solving ODEs forward in time at each training step, we approximate the integral of the learned rate functions directly using numerical quadrature. This yields an entirely algebraic forward pass consisting only of matrix operations, eliminating the repeated adaptive ODE solves of standard CRNN and producing smoother, more predictable training. We provide a recovery error analysis characterising the structural sources of ill-conditioning (conservation laws, reaction reversibility, and shared reactant sets) that limit network identifiability. On two benchmark CRNs, iCRNN trains in roughly half the wall-clock time of the baseline CRNN method on a four-species mechanism and between three and four times faster on a five-species mechanism, while completing every training run reliably and attaining comparable or lower loss.
items.title: Integral chemical reaction neural networks

items.summary: Traditional unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) methods are designed to flag or localise deviations from a normative distribution, ignoring the underlying generative mechanisms of the anomalies. Yet the nature of an anomaly is often as important as its presence. We reformulate UAD as a Bayesian inverse problem, in which the objective is to infer the most probable corruption responsible for each observation. Our framework yields a probabilistic anomaly score as the energy of the inferred corruption parameters, and serves as a principled recipe for developing new UAD algorithms. We derive several existing methods as instances of the general framework, each corresponding to the same energy score under different modelling choices. Experimentally, we study the framework's components in a controlled setting, and improve object-class AUROC on the MVTec AD dataset by 2.3% by adapting the underlying corruption model. Finally, we validate the framework on a brain MRI benchmark, achieving strong detection performance while producing estimates of pathology intensity, bias, and geometry. Code is available at https://github.com/jgmyles/inverse-uad.
items.title: A Principled Approach to Unsupervised Anomaly Detection

items.summary: This work studies whether internal rotation changes the longevity of source-free localized excitations in the reduced Enchan local time-rate field. The frozen scalar dynamics are S_tt = div[mu(D) grad S] - S with D = |grad S| and mu(D) = 1/(1 + D^(3/2)); no continuing external torque, centrifugal force, primitive matter source, or added rotational potential is used during the reported evolutions. Stage A supplies the non-rotating source-free baseline. Stage B1 initializes rotating phase-space states at omega = 4, 8, and 12 and evolves the extended runs to dimensionless time t = 100. Over 80 <= t <= 100, the mean localized-energy fractions are approximately 0.002207 for the non-rotating baseline and 0.006006, 0.149470, and 0.368846 for omega = 4, 8, and 12. The result is a graded rotation-associated longevity hierarchy: weak rotation gives little practical rescue, intermediate rotation substantially extends localization, and the strongest tested branch remains transient-localized through t = 100. Matched-energy near-zero-J_z controls provide a separate causality check and show that net canonical angular momentum alone is not a monotonic explanation of every late-time difference. Stage B2 separately tests spontaneous self-spin from exactly zero initial total angular momentum and finds no validated convergent counter-rotating branch in the tested scalar-only initial-data families. The ordered scan supports a physical formation picture in which a localized grain can move from weak rotational asymmetry through progressive spin-up into a strong-rotation long-lived branch. Time, space, and omega are dimensionless reduced-branch quantities; t = 100 is not assigned an SI duration in this work. The deposit contains the Version 1.0 manuscript PDF, a reproducibility ZIP with the publication source, code, selected archived numerical outputs, README, LICENSE, and SHA-256 integrity manifest. The final main.pdf is the default preview. License: Enchan Research & Verification License v1.0. Copyright (c) 2026 Mitsuhiro Kobayashi.
items.title: Can Rotation Make Spacetime Grains Last? Internal Angular Momentum and Longevity of Source-Free Enchan Grains

items.summary: Version 2.0.0 of the reproducibility archive for “Polynomial Iteration with Five-Moment Residual Certificates.” The archive contains source code, tests, row-level data, frozen numerical outputs, plotting code, provenance metadata, and checksums for the 108-case spectral benchmark, the observation-depth and boundary-moment diagnostics, and the 48-instance constrained predictive-control experiment. The numerical snapshot corresponds to the JOTA revision dated 20 September 2026. Code is distributed under the MIT License; data, numerical results, figures, and documentation are distributed under CC BY 4.0.
